messages:
kevin: Heads upfinance found ~30 credit events that never made it to NetSuite. They show up in Stripe as refunds/credit notes but our nightly apply job couldn't find them. Timing cluster around 2026-03-05 02:10-02:50 UTC.

maya: Any DLQ hits? We had a prune job change last week.

ops-bot: [auto] dlq-prune executed count_removed=120 window=2026-03-04..2026-03-05 rule=older_than_72h

kevin: That's my suspicion: the prune policy removed suppressed/delayed webhook payloads before the replay could process them. I see a handful of matching IDs in CloudWatch earlier but not in the S3 suppressed path.

finance-bot: [auto] mismatch-detect count=29 sample_invoices=[in_11Aaa,in_7Bb22] total_amount=5130

izzy: If DLQ pruning is the culprit, we need to recover payloads from Kinesis or retained logs. Do we have the raw webhook logs in log-archive?

maya: We keep 14 days of raw events in firehose -> s3://redwood-prod/webhooks/archive/yyyy-mm-dd/ but the archive job started after midnight; some events were only in dlq bucket for 48h before prune. Check s3://redwood-prod/webhooks/archive/2026-03-05/ and cloudtrail.

kevin: I ran `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-prod/webhooks/archive/2026-03-05/ | wc -l` -> 12,344. Grepping for invoice IDs shows 27 matching credit events. Good sign.

izzy: Great. Proposed plan: 1) ensure DLQ prune is paused 2) extract archive payloads for the affected window 3) run replay with --trace and --dry-run 4) reconcile with finance and apply. Ops folks: can we pause the prune rule?

ops-bot: [auto] dlq-prune toggle suggested by maya.

ops-bot: [auto] dlq-prune.paused_by=ops at=2026-03-06T08:12:02Z

maya: Paused. I've also raised the retention for suppressed bucket from 72h -> 14d in a hotfix config; will propose proper PR for review.

kevin: Extract commands I used:
```
# list archive files for interval
aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-prod --prefix "webhooks/archive/2026-03-05/" --query "Contents[?contains(Key,'invoice.payment_refund')].Key" > /tmp/keys.txt
# download matched keys
cat /tmp/keys.txt | xargs -n1 -P8 aws s3 cp s3://redwood-prod/ ./replay-2026-03-05/ --exclude "*" --include
# extract ids and write to ids.txt
python tools/extract_credit_ids.py --dir ./replay-2026-03-05/ > ids.txt
```

izzy: For replay run, use `--bypass-dlq-prune` and `--idempotency-check=strict`. We want to avoid duplicates. Also add annotations so finance can trace the original event -> ns_apply_id mapping.

support: Quick Q: if credits hit old invoices that closed in NetSuite, do we create memos or reopen invoices? Need policy before mass-apply.

finance-bot: [auto] policy-reminder: credits applied to closed invoices should create credit memos unless manual approval granted.

kevin: Good point. We'll run dry-run first and produce a CSV with columns: stripe_invoice, stripe_credit_id, net_suite_id_candidate, apply_action (memo|apply|skip), amount. Finance to approve for any 'memo' actions.

maya: Dry-run command I executed in staging:
```
python tools/replay_webhooks.py --ids-file ids.txt --dry-run --bypass-dlq-prune --annotate=original_event_ts > ./dryrun_2026-03-05.csv
```
Dry-run output: 27 processed -> 22 would apply as invoice credits; 5 flagged as create_memo (closed invoice) -> CSV uploaded to Google Drive: https://drive.redwood/replay-2026-03-05/dryrun.csv

kevin: Finance review needed. @support @izzy please don't run real apply until finance signs off on memos.

finance-bot: [auto] approval-request total=27 apply=22 memo=5 amount=5130 requested_by=kevin

izzy: Ops: schedule the real replay during low-traffic (03:30-04:00 UTC). I'll run it with `--idempotency-check=strict` and `--annotate=replay_job:dlq_recover_317`. We'll stream NetSuite apply confirmations to the replay logs for audit.

ops-bot: [auto] replay-job queued job_id=dlq_recover_317 window=2026-03-06T03:30:00Z queued_by=izzy

kevin: Finance approved the 22 applies; 5 memos require manual review by accounting (I've CC'd them on the CSV). Proceed after queue.

ops-bot: [auto] replay-job started job_id=dlq_recover_317 status=dry_run_started

maya: Dry-run confirms mapping to NS transaction numbers in candidates column. No conflicts found.

ops-bot: [auto] replay-job status=running job_id=dlq_recover_317

kevin: Running actual replay now with idempotency check. Command:
```
python tools/replay_webhooks.py --ids-file ids.txt --bypass-dlq-prune --annotate=replay_job:dlq_recover_317 --idempotency-check=strict
```

ops-bot: [auto] replay-job status=completed job_id=dlq_recover_317 applied=22 memos_created=5 skipped=0 failures=0 start=2026-03-06T03:31:10Z end=2026-03-06T03:44:05Z

finance-bot: [auto] reconcile-complete applied=22 memos=5 total_amount=5130 reconcile_id=rec_317

kevin: NetSuite applied IDs attached in ./replay_artifacts/rec_317_applies.csv. Finance confirmed balances reconcile and accounting will handle the memos.

izzy: Follow-ups: (1) revert DLQ retention to safe default but keep new 14d for suppressed webhook bucket, (2) add alert for dlq_prune removals >100/day, (3) add automated backfill check that looks for stripe credits without ns mapping daily. I'll open PRs.

support: I'll send customer comms for any customers whose invoices changed materially.

ops-bot: [auto] dlq-prune.resumed_by=ops at=2026-03-06T09:12:00Z with new-retention=suppressed:14d

kevin: Great work team. We'll include this incident in the monthly billing postmortem and add a runbook for DLQ recoveries. Closing once postmortem is in docs. :white_check_mark:
